name: management_accounts
intended_use: Run a declarative management-accounts engagement (chart, opening balances, entries and schedules) through the ledger kernel: statements, trial balance, two-route cash flow, closing and the retained-earnings rollforward, with every invariant checked.
unsupported_use: GAAP or IFRS statements; assurance; tax filings; multi-currency consolidation; posting anything the owner did not declare.
assumptions: Every entry is balanced and inside the period (enforced by the kernel).
The chart reflects the owner's account mapping.
Amounts respect the declared currency places.
limitations: Management accounts only: not GAAP or IFRS statements and not assurance (manual 9.5).
Cash-flow activity classification is a declared heuristic unless accounts carry explicit activity tags.
Custom analysis (T2); expert review pending.
The ledger engine decision is closed: the custom kernel is management accounts v1 (B-032, RESOLVED 2026-10-27); the Beancount comparison was never run.

spec.desc: the declarative engagement: period, currency, framework, places, chart, prior_closing, opening, entries, schedules

defaults.question: Reporting framework
defaults.default_chosen: A required input with no default (manual D-010).
defaults.impact: Standards differ by framework; none is asserted.

defaults.question: Closing
defaults.default_chosen: Every engagement closes: income, expenses and declared dividends move into retained earnings.
defaults.impact: Post-closing statements carry the period result in retained earnings.

defaults.question: Prior closing balances
defaults.default_chosen: A required input (an empty object for a first period); the opening entry is checked against it.
defaults.impact: A mismatch fails the opening-balances check.

name: trial_balance_check
intended_use: Compare a student's own trial balance with the one rebuilt from their own journal: every line that matches, differs or has no counterpart, with candidate causes labelled as heuristics.
unsupported_use: Deciding which of the two figures is correct; checking amounts against source documents; detecting an error of principle that the journal itself encodes; correcting anything.
assumptions: Both inputs are the student's own declared figures.
An account code, where given, means the same account on both sides.
limitations: A balanced trial balance is not proof of correct entries: errors of principle, commission, original entry, omission, reversal and compensating errors all leave it balanced.
Candidate causes are heuristics labelled as such, never conclusions.
It cannot check amounts against source documents, and it corrects nothing.
Custom analysis (T2); expert review pending.

journal.desc: the student's journal in the engagement shape (period, chart, opening, entries); optional, and supplying it is what makes the check meaningful

trial_balance.desc: the student's own trial balance rows: a code or a name, and a debit or a credit

places.desc: decimal places the figures were stated to (default 2)

defaults.question: Matching an account
defaults.default_chosen: By account code when both sides carry one, otherwise by name; an ambiguous name is refused rather than resolved.
defaults.impact: A shared name would otherwise be matched arbitrarily.

defaults.question: Which figure is right
defaults.default_chosen: Neither. The check compares two declared figures and does not decide between them.
defaults.impact: The verdict names where they disagree, never which is correct.

name: ratio_analysis
intended_use: Compute liquidity, profitability, solvency and efficiency ratios from figures on your own financial statements, showing each ratio's declared formula and the figures it used.
unsupported_use: Benchmarks, industry averages or pass/fail judgements; GAAP or IFRS presentation; restating or adjusting figures; multi-period comparatives; segment, consolidated or multi-currency analysis; forecasting.
assumptions: The figures are as reported for one period, in one currency and on one accounting basis.
Balance-sheet figures are period-end balances.
limitations: Descriptive arithmetic only; no benchmark, threshold or verdict is applied because none is supplied or verified.
The figures are not validated against a trial balance here; use the management-accounts method for a bookkeeping-level check.
There is no tax computation; net income is used exactly as supplied.

current_assets.desc: current assets at the period end

current_liabilities.desc: current liabilities at the period end

cost_of_sales.desc: cost of sales for the period

net_income.desc: net income for the period (as supplied; no tax computation is performed)

interest_expense.desc: interest expense for the period, as a positive amount

defaults.question: Benchmarks and cut-offs
defaults.default_chosen: None are applied, because none is supplied or verified. Ratios are computed, not rated.
defaults.impact: Whether a value is good or bad is left to the reader and the context.

defaults.question: Balance conventions
defaults.default_chosen: Period-end balances and a 365-day year for the efficiency ratios.
defaults.impact: Average balances or a 360-day year would give different numbers.

defaults.question: Uncomputable ratios
defaults.default_chosen: A ratio with a missing figure or a zero denominator is listed in the appendix with its reason and is not estimated.
defaults.impact: The pack is partial rather than invented.

name: standard_cost_variances
intended_use: Material price and usage, labour rate and efficiency, and (when declared) variable and fixed overhead variances for the output actually produced, with a positive figure unfavourable.
unsupported_use: Setting or judging standards; mix, yield, sales, planning or idle-capacity variances; standard costing in several processes or products; tax or inventory valuation effects.
assumptions: The standards are the declared quantities and prices.
Actual hours and quantities are for the same period and output.
limitations: No standards setting, mix, yield, sales or planning variances.
One product and one process only.
No journal entries or inventory valuation.

actual_units.desc: units actually produced in the period

standard_material_per_unit.desc: standard material quantity allowed per unit

standard_material_price.desc: standard price per unit of material

actual_material_price.desc: actual price paid per unit of material

standard_hours_per_unit.desc: standard labour hours allowed per unit

standard_variable_overhead_rate.desc: optional standard variable overhead per labour hour

actual_variable_overhead.desc: actual variable overhead, required with the standard rate

budgeted_fixed_overhead.desc: optional budgeted fixed overhead for the period

actual_fixed_overhead.desc: actual fixed overhead, required with the budget

denominator_hours.desc: budgeted labour hours used to set the fixed overhead rate

defaults.question: Sign convention
defaults.default_chosen: Every variance is actual cost less the standard cost of the output achieved; positive is unfavourable.
defaults.impact: A different convention flips every sign and the favourable/unfavourable reading.

defaults.question: Overhead detail
defaults.default_chosen: Variable and fixed overhead variances are reported only when their inputs are declared.
defaults.impact: Leaving them out reports material and labour only.

name: abc_costing
intended_use: Activity-based costing: a rate per activity from its pool and driver total, each product's allocation from the driver quantities it consumes, and the resulting unit cost.
unsupported_use: Choosing cost drivers; idle or unused capacity cost; activity hierarchies; time-driven ABC; cost of poor quality.
assumptions: Pool costs and driver quantities are declared for one period.
Every product's driver quantities are recorded for every activity it consumes.
limitations: No idle-capacity adjustment, activity hierarchy or time-driven ABC.
One period and one currency.
The drivers are the declared ones, not chosen or validated.

activities.desc: one record per activity pool: a name and its cost

products.desc: one record per product: a name and its units produced

allocations.desc: one record per activity-product pair: the driver quantity that product consumed

defaults.question: Pool allocation
defaults.default_chosen: Every pool is allocated in full over the driver quantities declared, with no unused-capacity cost.
defaults.impact: Leaving idle capacity in the pool overstates product cost.

defaults.question: Driver totals
defaults.default_chosen: Driver totals are the sum of the declared product quantities, not a separate capacity figure.
defaults.impact: Using practical capacity would need a separate driver total.

name: sales_variances
intended_use: Sales price, mix and yield variances for two or more products, at budgeted prices with the budget mix as the standard, reconciling to the total revenue change.
unsupported_use: Explaining why price or mix moved; market-size and market-share variances; a changing standard; more than one period.
assumptions: Budget and actual units and prices cover the same period and product set.
The budget mix is the standard mix.
limitations: No market-size or share variance; no explanation of the movements.
The split depends on the declared convention.
One currency and one period.

products.desc: one record per product with budget and actual units and prices

defaults.question: Standard mix
defaults.default_chosen: The budget mix is the standard, and mix and yield are valued at budgeted prices.
defaults.impact: A different standard or valuation changes the split, not the total.

defaults.question: Scope
defaults.default_chosen: One period and the products declared; no market-size or market-share split.
defaults.impact: Those need the market total, which is not declared here.

name: breakeven
intended_use: Units needed to cover fixed cost at a constant unit contribution, with the break-even revenue, contribution margin, margin of safety and target-profit volume when those inputs are declared.
unsupported_use: Multi-product mix; step-fixed costs; non-linear price or cost; a demand response to the price; tax; financing cost.
assumptions: Linear cost and revenue.
The expected volume is the owner's declared input, not a forecast.
limitations: Single product; a mix needs multi_product_breakeven.
No tax, financing or working-capital effects.
The margin of safety is relative to the declared expected volume only.

expected_units.desc: optional expected sales volume, for the margin of safety

target_profit.desc: optional pre-tax profit target, for the required volume

defaults.question: Cost behavior
defaults.default_chosen: Fixed cost is constant and unit price and variable cost are constant.
defaults.impact: Break-even moves if costs are stepped or prices change with volume.

defaults.question: Margin of safety and target profit
defaults.default_chosen: Both are reported only when expected_units or target_profit is declared; neither is assumed.
defaults.impact: A different expected volume changes the margin of safety but not the break-even point.

name: multi_product_breakeven
intended_use: Break-even in units and revenue for a fixed product mix: the mix-weighted contribution margin and the per-product break-even quantities.
unsupported_use: A changing mix, step costs, capacity limits, price-volume relationships or tax; forecasting which mix will actually occur.
assumptions: Each product's price and variable cost are constant.
The declared mix is the mix that will be sold.
Fixed costs do not change with volume.
limitations: One break-even point for one declared mix; no capacity limits or step costs.
No tax, financing or working-capital effects.
Per-product units are a break-even mix, not a target.

fixed_costs.desc: total fixed costs for the period

products.desc: two or more products with a declared mix (mix_units are the relative quantities sold)

defaults.question: Mix assumption
defaults.default_chosen: The declared mix_units are held constant and used as the weighting.
defaults.impact: A different mix changes the weighted contribution and the break-even.

defaults.question: Cost behaviour
defaults.default_chosen: Fixed costs are constant and unit prices and variable costs are constant over the range.
defaults.impact: Step costs or volume discounts break the single break-even point.

name: working_capital
intended_use: Measure the cash conversion cycle from receivable, inventory and payable days, and compute the economic order quantity, reorder point and the annualised cost of forgoing a trade discount.
unsupported_use: Forecasting working capital; seasonal or step demand; quantity discounts; bad-debt and credit-scoring models; a full cash budget.
assumptions: The period-end balances and the annual demand are the owner's figures.
Demand, order cost and holding cost are constant over the year.
The credit terms are as declared.
limitations: No seasonality, quantity discounts or stock-out cost.
No cash budget or forecast.
The trade-credit cost is an annualised convention, not a financing recommendation.

cost_of_sales.desc: cost of sales for the period

receivables.desc: trade receivables at the period end

payables.desc: trade payables at the period end

annual_demand.desc: units demanded in a year, for the order quantity

holding_cost_per_unit.desc: cost of holding one unit for a year

discount_percent.desc: early-payment discount as a decimal, e.g. 0.02 for 2%; use 0 if there is none

credit_terms_days.desc: full credit period in days, e.g. 30

discount_days.desc: days within which the discount must be taken, e.g. 10

daily_demand.desc: units sold per day; default annual demand divided by days

lead_time_days.desc: supplier lead time in days; default 0

defaults.question: Which balances?
defaults.default_chosen: Period-end balances and a 365-day year; average balances would give different days.
defaults.impact: A seasonal business can look very different at a peak or trough date.

defaults.question: Inventory model
defaults.default_chosen: A constant-demand EOQ with a fixed order cost and holding cost per unit.
defaults.impact: Quantity discounts and step costs change the optimal order size.

name: loan_amortization
intended_use: Compute the level payment on an amortizing loan, the total interest over its life, the first payment's interest and principal split, and the effective annual rate.
unsupported_use: Variable or teaser rates; interest-only or balloon structures; fees, insurance or prepayment penalties; a full period-by-period schedule export.
assumptions: The rate is fixed for the whole term.
Payments are level and made on time.
The loan is fully amortized with no balloon.
limitations: No variable, capped or teaser rates.
No fees, insurance, taxes or penalties.
No period-by-period schedule; only the first split and the totals are reported.

annual_rate.desc: nominal ANNUAL interest rate as a decimal, e.g. 0.09 for 9%

payments_per_year.desc: number of payments a year; default 12 (monthly)

defaults.question: Payment frequency
defaults.default_chosen: Monthly payments (12 a year); every other frequency can be declared.
defaults.impact: More frequent payments reduce the interest paid over the life.

defaults.question: Rate convention
defaults.default_chosen: The annual rate is divided by the number of payments a year; the effective annual rate is reported separately.
defaults.impact: A quoted monthly rate entered as annual would be wrong by a factor of twelve.

name: trend_analysis
intended_use: Turn several years of income-statement figures into common-size percentages, an index on the first period, compound growth rates and margin changes.
unsupported_use: Forecasting; adjusting or restating the figures; industry benchmarks; segment or consolidated analysis; balance-sheet common-size beyond the equity-to-assets ratio; more than ten periods.
assumptions: Revenue is positive in every period, because it is the common-size base.
The periods are consecutive and in increasing order.
The figures are as reported, on one accounting basis and in one currency.
limitations: Historical arithmetic only; no adjustment, restatement or forecast.
CAGR uses only the endpoints and ignores the path.
A net-income CAGR is omitted when the base period's net income is not positive.

years.desc: the period labels, in increasing order, e.g. 2022, 2023, 2024

revenue.desc: revenue for each period, in the same order

cost_of_sales.desc: cost of sales for each period

net_income.desc: net income for each period; may be negative

total_assets.desc: optional total assets per period, for equity-to-assets and asset growth

equity.desc: optional equity per period, supplied with total_assets

defaults.question: Which base?
defaults.default_chosen: Revenue is the common-size base and the first declared period is the index base (100).
defaults.impact: A different base changes every percentage but not the underlying figures.

defaults.question: Growth measure
defaults.default_chosen: Both the compound rate across the whole span and the latest period-on-period change are reported, so they are not confused.
defaults.impact: A single endpoint can move the CAGR sharply.

name: tax_declared
intended_use: Income tax, VAT payable and deferred tax from the rates and figures you declare, with the after-tax income and the total tax charge.
unsupported_use: Any jurisdiction's tax law: credits, exemptions, thresholds, progressive bands, NOLCO, withholding, filing, penalties or refunds. It does not derive taxable income from the accounts.
assumptions: The declared taxable income and rates are the ones that apply to the period.
VAT output and input are for the same period and the same registration.
limitations: No credits, exemptions, thresholds, progressive bands, NOLCO, withholding or filing rules.
No link to the accounting profit or the statements.
Deferred tax is one declared difference times one declared rate.

taxable_income.desc: the taxable income you declare; a loss can be entered as a negative figure

income_tax_rate.desc: the income tax rate as a decimal, e.g. 0.25 for 25%

vat_input_tax.desc: optional input VAT on purchases, declared with the output VAT

temporary_difference.desc: optional temporary difference for deferred tax

deferred_tax_rate.desc: the deferred tax rate, declared with the temporary difference

defaults.question: Jurisdiction
defaults.default_chosen: None. The rates and the taxable income are yours; the method applies no national or local tax law.
defaults.impact: A real filing needs the jurisdiction's rules and a tax adviser.

defaults.question: Taxable income
defaults.default_chosen: The declared figure is used as given; a loss carries no positive income tax and no loss carry-forward.
defaults.impact: A carry-forward or minimum tax needs the jurisdiction's rules.
